featured_reviews.review_text:
If you have ever watched your parent live with constant knee pain, trying one medicine after another, hoping and praying for relief but never truly getting better, you will understand exactly how I feel today.

For 10–12 years, my mother suffered from advanced arthritis. She was homebound, struggled to walk, couldn’t climb stairs, and slowly began losing hope that she would ever regain a normal, pain-free life. Surgery had been suggested years ago, but she was never fully confident. So she kept postponing it, hoping something else would work.

Then we met Dr. Sachin Rathod.

From our very first consultation, we felt we were in the right place. He was warm, patient, and incredibly easy to talk to. We did not feel rushed. He answered every question calmly, explained the entire process clearly, and most importantly, gave us realistic expectations. He didn’t push us, he gave us clarity and confidence to decide.

In today’s world, where many doctors seem rushed or inaccessible, Dr. Rathod is truly different. If you want someone who listens—really listens - he is that doctor. You can openly discuss health concerns, risks, costs, pre-operative and post-operative doubts - anything. He responds personally. Not through assistants. Not after days of waiting. Often within minutes or a few hours, and it is always him. That level of accessibility and dedication is rare.

One incident truly touched us. He had promised to visit my mother one day but was held up due to other commitments. We assumed he might not make it. Yet, late that night, he came—just as promised. He didn’t rush. He spent time with her, examined her carefully, reassured her, and patiently answered our concerns. That moment showed us that his commitment goes far beyond routine duty.

Initially, we thought we would take a second opinion and wait another month or two. But after meeting him, we were certain. Within two weeks of completing the required tests (which he had already guided us about during our first visit), my mother underwent bilateral total knee replacement surgery.

The surgery lasted five hours.
When she came out, something had changed; not just physically, but mentally. She was positive and motivated. Dr. Rathod was not just a surgeon; he was a counselor, guide, and motivator.

His care did not end after surgery. He personally made her walk on the first day. On the second day, she even climbed a couple of steps. For all four days in the hospital, he remained present and involved. He never disappeared after the procedure or delegated everything to assistants.

Even during recovery, he stayed accessible. We could send reports on WhatsApp, clarify doubts anytime, and receive guidance promptly. In this busy digital age, having a doctor who is reachable, responsive, and completely ego-free is remarkable.

Within just 6-7 days, my mother was able to bend her knees up to 85–90 degrees. Even the physiotherapist mentioned that this reflected excellent surgical technique and precision.

But beyond the medical success, what moves me most is this: for as long as I remember, my mother’s legs were bent due to arthritis. Today, they are straight. She is walking again with strength, confidence, and hope. It truly feels like she has been given a new set of knees and a renewed mindset.

If you are watching your parent suffer from severe knee pain, please do not hesitate to consult Dr. Sachin Rathod. He will listen. He will guide you honestly. And he will stand by you, not just during surgery, but beyond it.

He is not just an exceptional orthopedic surgeon, he is a compassionate human being.

We are deeply grateful.

Shin splints are a common cause of lower leg pain, especially among runners, athletes, and fitness enthusiasts. The pain is usually felt along the inner edge of the shin bone and may worsen during or after activity.

What Orthopedic Surgeons Evaluate Before Recommending Knee Replacement

Knee replacement surgery is not the first step in treating knee pain. An experienced orthopedic surgeon carefully evaluates several important factors before recommending surgery.

First, the severity of arthritis or joint damage is assessed through X-rays or MRI scans. Surgery is usually considered when there is advanced cartilage loss, bone-on-bone arthritis, or deformity.

Second, the level of pain and functional limitation matters. If knee pain affects daily activities like walking, climbing stairs, or sleeping—and does not improve with medications or physiotherapy—surgery may be advised.

Third, the response to conservative treatment is reviewed. Most patients are initially treated with medication, lifestyle changes, injections, or physiotherapy before considering knee replacement.

Age, activity level, overall health, weight, and medical conditions such as diabetes or heart disease are also evaluated to ensure safe surgery and better recovery.

Dr. Mohit Kukreja, an experienced Knee Replacement Surgeon in Mumbai and Orthopedic Surgeon in Mumbai, follows a patient-specific approach. He recommends knee replacement only when non-surgical treatments no longer provide relief and the goal is to restore mobility and improve quality of life.

When Both Knees Hurt: Should You Consider Bilateral Knee Replacement?

Pain in both knees can make everyday activities like walking, standing, or climbing stairs extremely difficult. When medications, injections, and physiotherapy no longer provide relief, bilateral knee replacement may be a treatment option worth considering.

Bilateral knee replacement involves treating both knee joints, either in one surgery or in a planned staged approach. It is usually advised for patients with severe arthritis or advanced joint damage affecting both knees equally.

According to Dr. Mohit Kukreja, Knee Replacement Surgeon in Mumbai and Orthopedic Surgeon in Mumbai, bilateral surgery can offer balanced recovery, improved walking alignment, and a single rehabilitation period for selected patients. However, it is not suitable for everyone. A patient’s age, overall health, heart condition, bone strength, and ability to undergo rehabilitation are carefully evaluated before recommending this option.

In some cases, operating on one knee at a time may be safer and more appropriate. The right decision depends on a detailed clinical assessment and personalized treatment planning.

How a Small Rotator Cuff Tear Becomes a Big Problem When Ignored

Many people ignore mild shoulder pain, assuming it’s just a strain or stiffness that will settle on its own. However, a small rotator cuff tear, if left untreated, can gradually turn into a major shoulder problem.

The rotator cuff is a group of tendons that helps lift and rotate your arm. When a small tear is ignored, continued daily activities, repetitive movements, or lifting can cause the tear to increase in size. Over time, this leads to worsening pain, weakness, difficulty lifting the arm, and disturbed sleep—especially night pain.

As the tear enlarges, surrounding muscles weaken and shoulder movement becomes restricted. What could have been managed with early treatment or physiotherapy may eventually require arthroscopic surgery. Delayed care can also slow recovery and reduce the chances of full shoulder function.

Early diagnosis with proper clinical examination and imaging is key. Timely treatment helps prevent long-term damage and restores shoulder strength and mobility.

Dr. Mohit Kukreja, Arthroscopic Surgeon in Mumbai and Orthopedic Surgeon in Mumbai, emphasizes that early evaluation of persistent shoulder pain can prevent small rotator cuff tears from becoming complex surgical problems.

If shoulder pain lasts more than a few weeks, don’t ignore it—early care makes all the difference.

How Delaying Hip Replacement Affects Spine, Knee, and Overall Posture

Hip pain is often tolerated for years with painkillers, injections, or activity restriction. However, delaying hip replacement surgery doesn’t just affect the hip joint—it gradually impacts the spine, knees, and overall posture.

When the hip joint is damaged, the body automatically changes the way it walks to reduce pain. This abnormal walking pattern puts extra stress on the opposite knee, lower back, and spine. Over time, patients may develop knee pain, back stiffness, disc problems, and visible posture changes such as limping or bending to one side.

As hip movement reduces, the spine compensates by working harder, leading to chronic back pain. Similarly, the knee on the unaffected side bears extra load, increasing the risk of early arthritis.

According to Dr. Mohit Kukreja, Hip Replacement Surgeon in Mumbai and Hip Surgeon in Mumbai, timely hip replacement can restore proper alignment, improve walking mechanics, and prevent secondary joint damage.

Hip replacement is not just about pain relief—it’s about protecting the rest of the body and restoring natural movement. Early intervention often leads to better recovery, improved posture, and a more active, pain-free life.

The Pain You Ignore Today Becomes the Surgery Tomorrow: Early Signs of Sports Injuries Athletes Miss

Many athletes and fitness enthusiasts believe that playing through pain is a sign of strength. In reality, it is often the first step toward a serious sports injury. What starts as mild discomfort can silently progress into ligament tears, cartilage damage, or stress fractures—eventually requiring surgery.

Early warning signs that are commonly ignored include persistent pain after workouts, swelling that doesn’t settle, stiffness in the morning, reduced range of motion, and pain that worsens with activity. These symptoms often indicate underlying damage that needs timely attention.

Overuse injuries are especially dangerous because they develop gradually. Ignoring them can lead to chronic conditions that affect performance and long-term joint health.

According to Dr. Mohit Kukreja, Sports Injury Specialist in Mumbai and Orthopedic Surgeon in Mumbai, early diagnosis and proper treatment can prevent most sports injuries from progressing to surgery. Rest, physiotherapy, activity modification, and targeted rehabilitation at the right time can make a huge difference.

featured_reviews.name: Akshay Jain
featured_reviews.review_text:
I underwent right ankle surgery under Dr. Ajay Shenvi. My family and friends have also consulted him in the past. I have absolutely no complaints about the doctor—he is excellent at his work and highly skilled.

However, I would advise patients and families to be cautious when dealing with the hospital staff. If you are making any payment, ensure that you receive an invoice for the exact amount paid. I understand that patients and their families are already under stress during such times, but unfortunately, some staff members seem to take advantage of this situation.

I paid approximately INR 1,80,000 for my surgery, but the invoice provided was for around INR 1,79,000. Initially, I discussed this with my family and decided to let it go. During my follow-up appointment after 15 days, I raised this issue with the reception. She initially asked me to prove the INR 1,000 difference, and once I showed the details, she suddenly acknowledged the discrepancy and redirected me to the ward nurse.

The ward nurse also appeared aware that an extra INR 1,000 had been collected and gave several unnecessary explanations. Although I considered discussing this with the doctor, I chose not to involve him. Eventually, I received a refund after my follow-up visit. The staff claimed they had noted it in their diary but forgot to inform me for 15 days, which is difficult to believe. They both were giving me unnecessary excuses and was making me feel that I am wrong because I raised after 15 days and in their view it is too late. They forgot that I underwent surgery and need some time for recovery. Really disappointed with the both staff and their behaviour for INR 1000.

The takeaway is simple: always verify your invoices and payment receipts. Do not assume everything is accurate—double-check the amounts you pay to them.
